claims.text: Procopius describes Vitigis’s court under siege and Belisarius’s capture, custody and claim on palace money for the emperor. Sarris separately describes Justinian’s imperial office and disputed Egyptian tax oversight. Royal negotiation, military capture and fiscal supervision are different relations. Neither an imperial participant’s account nor an edict establishes universal consent or effortless control.
